1	# Plan d'implémentation : S-02b (DEVDESK-711) — arrêt propre d'abord (Linux, macOS), puis forcer sur confirmation
2	
3	Une seule PR, branche `feat/safe-process-stop-s02b`, base `origin/main` ec457184 (S-01a, S-02a, S-01b, bug 714 fusionnés).
4	Spécification : `docs/product/safe-process-stop/stories.md`, S-02b (7 critères, contrainte Rule 110 / tick ~250 ms / génération). Non rediscutée.
5	Plans précédents : `DEVDESK-708-plan.md` (seams, `realOS.kill`, `pendingKill`), `DEVDESK-709-plan.md` (`Identity`, `ConfirmIdentity`, `refusal`, `targetPresence`).
6	
7	## 0. Ce que dit le code aujourd'hui (lu le 2026-11-23, `main` ec457184)
8	
9	- `internal/ports/procos.go` : seams `selfPID`, `parentPID`, `goos`, `now`, `procOS osProcs = realOS{}`. `osProcs` = `createTime`, `identity(pid) (uint64, error)`, `kill(pid, want Identity) error`. `realOS.kill` : `refuseRealSignalUnderTest` (1re instruction) → `os.FindProcess` (pidfd Linux ≥ 5.4, handle Windows) → `heldIdentity` → `verdictAtSignal` → `p.Kill()`.
10	- `internal/ports/ports.go` : `Kill(pid string, listed Identity) error` = `parsePID` → `protectionOf` → `n <= 0` → identité connue sinon `*UnverifiableError` → `procOS.kill` enveloppé `killing process N: %w`.
11	- `internal/ports/identity.go` : `parseStartTicks` (champs comptés après la dernière `)`), `verdictAtSignal`, `ConfirmIdentity`. Lecteurs par OS : `identity_{linux,darwin,windows,other}.go` (`readIdentity`, `heldIdentity`, `isNoSuchProcess`). macOS lit `unix.SysctlKinfoProc("kern.proc.pid", pid)`.
12	- `internal/ports/signal_guard_test.go` : `TestOnlyRealOSSendsASignal` refuse `FindProcess`, `Kill`, `Signal`, `TerminateProcess` (nom du sélecteur) hors de `(realOS) kill`, dont la 1re instruction doit être `refuseRealSignalUnderTest`.
13	- `internal/ui/netdiag/ports_commands.go` : `processOps{protection, confirm, kill, windows}`, `killProcessCmd(kill, t)`, `portsRefreshMsg`, `requestPortsRefresh()`.
14	- `internal/ui/netdiag/ports_model.go` (679 lignes) : `confirmKill` (gardes → `ops.confirm` → `pendingKill` → modale `Kill Process` / `killPrompt`), `handleConfirmYes` (`targetPresence` → protection → busy → `MarkBusy("Killing …")` → `killProcessCmd`), `handleKillResult` (`ClearBusy`, `refusal`, Info `Process N terminated`), `refusal` (classement unique), `killable()` (ligne → PID → protection → identité), `killPrompt(t, windows)`, `killHelpDescription(windows)`. `esc` n'a aucun rôle sur l'onglet Ports aujourd'hui (`handleKeyNormal` ne le traite pas ; la modale le traduit en `ConfirmModalNoMsg`).
15	- `internal/ui/netdiag/update.go` : les messages Ports sont aiguillés par type (`case portsTickMsg, portsDataMsg, portsKillResultMsg, portsRefreshMsg`), quel que soit l'onglet actif ; `jobs.FrameMsg` pousse la phase de clignotement au tableau Ports ; `routeConfirm` envoie Yes/No à Forward si l'onglet actif est Forward, sinon à Ports.
16	- `internal/ui/netdiag/ports_activity.go` : `WantsBlink()` vrai tant qu'une marque busy existe (le point de la ligne clignote).
17	- `internal/ui/netdiag/header.go` : `K` « Kill process » (grisé par `killable()`), aide « Ports Tab — How it works » et `killHelpDescription`.
18	- `internal/ui/netdiag/view.go` : la modale Ports est posée par `lipgloss.Place` ; `ConfirmModal.View()` ne replie pas les lignes (padding 2 + bordure 1 de chaque côté).
19	- **Routeur** (`internal/app/app.go`) : un message non reconnu va à la vue **active** (`forwardToActiveView`). Si l'utilisateur quitte `:net` pendant un kill, `portsKillResultMsg` est perdu et la ligne reste busy (défaut existant, non signalé) ; `routeToView` existe pour router vers une vue hors écran. `Running()` de netdiag protège la vue d'une suppression (`command_line.go:161`).
20	- Aucun appelant de `ports.Kill` hors de netdiag ; le MCP (`internal/mcp/ports_tools.go`) n'appelle que `ports.List`.
21	
22	Vérifié dans les sources :
23	- Go 1.27.4 `os/exec_unix.go` : `(*Process).signal` passe par `pidfdSendSignal` quand un pidfd est tenu, sinon `kill(2)` ; `p.Signal(syscall.SIGTERM)` bénéficie donc de la même garantie « processus tenu » que `p.Kill()`. `ESRCH` → `os.ErrProcessDone`, `EPERM` → `errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission)`.
24	- `syscall.SIGTERM` existe sous Windows (`syscall/types_windows.go`) : `realOS.kill` compile partout ; `os.Process.Signal` y rend une erreur « not supported », jamais atteinte (section 3.2).
25	- `golang.org/x/sys v0.49.0` darwin : `KinfoProc.Proc.P_stat int8` existe ; **aucune constante `SZOMB` exportée** → constante locale `darwinSZOMB = 5` (`<sys/proc.h>` : SIDL 1, SRUN 2, SSLEEP 3, SSTOP 4, SZOMB 5).
26	- `testutil.FastTimers(t, *time.Duration)` ramène une durée à 1 ms pour un test.
27	
28	## 1. Exigences non fonctionnelles
29	
30	- **Sûreté** : jamais de SIGKILL sans la seconde confirmation (critère 3). Chaque signal (SIGTERM puis SIGKILL) passe par le même `realOS.kill`, processus tenu, avec la même vérification d'identité contre l'identité capturée à la confirmation (critère 5). La sonde n'envoie **aucun** signal (pas même le signal 0).
31	- **Réactivité (Rule 110)** : aucune attente bloquante ; l'attente est une chaîne de `tea.Tick` (250 ms) dont chaque tick sonde et renvoie un message portant une génération ; seul `Update` modifie le modèle.
32	- **Coût** : au plus ~21 sondes par arrêt (une lecture de `/proc/<pid>/stat` sous Linux, un `sysctl` sous macOS) ; aucune lecture au rendu.
33	- **Portabilité** : `GOOS=linux|darwin|windows` compilent, `go vet` et `go test -c` passent pour les trois. Windows : comportement S-02a **inchangé**.
34	- **Exploitabilité** : logs `log.Printf("ERROR [netdiag/ports] …")` pour une sonde illisible ; `INFO` quand un zombie est compté arrêté.
35	- **Tests sans vrai signal** : tout par seams ; vrais signaux seulement sur des enfants lancés par le test (`allowRealSignals`), Linux.
36	
37	## 2. Options comparées
38	
39	### 2.1 Où vit l'attente
40	
41	| Option | Pour | Contre |
42	|---|---|---|
43	| A. Dans `internal/ports` : `StopGracefully(pid, id, 5s)` bloquant dans un `Cmd` | Une seule fonction | Un `Cmd` qui dort 5 s : `esc` ne peut pas l'interrompre sans contexte, la seconde confirmation est un état UI, la génération perd son sens ; contraire à la contrainte de conception |
44	| **B. Machine à états dans `netdiag`, primitives sans état dans `ports` (recommandée)** : `ports.Terminate`, `ports.Probe`, `ports.Kill` ; le modèle tient l'arrêt en cours, une chaîne de ticks sonde | Conforme à la contrainte (tick + sonde + génération) ; chaque primitive testable seule ; `ports` ne connaît ni l'UI ni le temps | Plus de messages côté UI |
45	
46	### 2.2 Envoyer SIGTERM
47	
48	| Option | Pour | Contre |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| **A. `realOS.kill(pid, want, sig)` reçoit le signal à envoyer (recommandée)** | Un seul point d'envoi, une seule vérification d'identité pour les deux signaux (critère 5) ; le garde statique et le garde à l'exécution restent **inchangés** (`p.Signal` et `p.Kill` dans `(realOS) kill`) | La méthode s'appelle toujours `kill` alors qu'elle peut envoyer SIGTERM (commentaire) |

94	- **Un seul arrêt en attente** : `pm.stop *pendingStop` (nil = aucun). Phases `signalling`, `waiting`, `askingForce`, `forcing`. `pendingKill` reste la cible de la **première** confirmation (inchangé, Windows inclus).
95	- **Génération** : chaque arrêt reçoit `gen = nextStopGen()` (compteur `atomic.Uint64` de paquet, unique même entre deux modèles netdiag reconstruits). Tout message d'arrêt dont `gen` ≠ `pm.stop.gen`, ou reçu quand `pm.stop == nil`, ou dans une phase qui ne l'attend pas, est **ignoré** sans effet. `esc` met `pm.stop = nil` : le tick en vol devient périmé ; un nouvel arrêt lancé aussitôt a une autre génération, donc l'ancien tick ne le touche pas.
96	- **Échéance** : `deadline = msg.at + stopGrace`, `at` étant l'instant où le `Cmd` du SIGTERM a rendu ; chaque `portsStopProbeMsg` porte l'instant du tick (`tea.Tick` le fournit). Aucune horloge dans le modèle : les tests fixent `at`.
97	- **Sonde illisible** (erreur autre que « parti ») : journalisée, comptée **vivante** (aucune fausse annonce « stopped ») ; l'échéance amène la seconde confirmation, dont le SIGKILL revérifie l'identité.
98	- **Seconde étape** (`Yes`) : `targetPresence(target)` → `replaced` : `refusal(IdentityChangedError)` (critère 5, sans appel système) ; `absent` **n'arrête pas** la seconde étape (un processus qui s'arrête ferme souvent ses sockets avant de sortir ; c'est le cas même que la seconde étape doit traiter — l'identité est revérifiée au signal) ; protection recalculée ; puis SIGKILL par `pm.ops.kill(pid, target.Identity)`.
99	- **Résultat du SIGKILL d'un arrêt en deux temps** : `os.ErrProcessDone` → Info `x (N) stopped` (le processus est sorti de lui-même entre l'échéance et `Yes` ; décision proposée, plus juste que l'Error `PID N is no longer running`) ; `IdentityChangedError` → texte S-01b critère 2 + relecture (critère 5) ; le reste par `refusal` ; succès → Info `Process N terminated` (inchangé).
100	- **Pendant l'attente** : le tableau continue de se rafraîchir (chaîne `portsTickMsg` indépendante, la pause `space` reste un choix de l'utilisateur), toutes les touches répondent ; la chaîne de sonde n'est pas suspendue quand le terminal perd le focus (5 s bornées).
101	- **Windows** : `pm.stop` n'est **jamais** posé. `handleConfirmYes` garde exactement le chemin S-02a (`MarkBusy("Killing …")` + `killProcessCmd(kill, t, 0)`), sélectionné par `pm.ops.windows` (lui-même `runtime.GOOS == "windows"` en production, injecté en test). Aucune attente, aucune seconde confirmation, aucun texte nouveau.

334	### 3.5 Règles d'interface
335	
336	- **Rule 110** : `terminateCmd`, `stopProbeCmd`, `killProcessCmd` ne lisent pas le modèle ; toutes les transitions sont dans `Update`.
337	- **Rule 130** : la liste des raccourcis d'un même écran ne change pas d'un état à l'autre (`esc` toujours présent sous Unix, grisé hors attente). `K` grisé pendant un arrêt est une **exception assumée** à « une opération en cours n'est pas une cause de grisé » : imposée par le critère 7, l'état dure au plus 5 s puis une modale, et la raison s'affiche à l'appui (Warn). Le pied de page montre le libellé seulement si la ligne sélectionnée est celle de l'arrêt (`rowDetail`, inchangé).
340	- **Rule 114** : aide mise à jour dans le même commit.

526	## 6. Hypothèses, risques, irréversible
527	
528	**Hypothèses non vérifiées.**
529	- H1 : un zombie Linux garde `starttime` dans `/proc/<pid>/stat` (proc(5)) — vérifié par `TestProbeSeesARealZombie`.
530	- H2 : sous macOS, `kern.proc.pid` rend un zombie avec `P_stat == SZOMB (5)` et son `P_starttime`. Non exécuté. Si faux, le zombie se lit « parti » : compté arrêté dans les deux cas.
531	- H3 : `darwinSZOMB = 5` (valeur de `<sys/proc.h>`, non exportée par `x/sys`).
532	- H4 : sous macOS, SIP peut refuser SIGTERM → `EPERM` → message existant (critère 6).
533	- H5 : `tea.Tick` appelle son callback dans la goroutine du `Cmd` (la sonde y est faite) — conforme à l'usage actuel de bubbletea v2.
534	
535	**Risques.**
536	- **Modale hors de vue** : l'échéance peut ouvrir la 2e confirmation pendant que l'utilisateur est sur un autre onglet ou une autre vue ; il la retrouve sur Ports. Rien n'est forcé sans elle (critère 3 tenu), mais l'utilisateur peut ne pas savoir qu'elle attend. Limite documentée.
537	- **Reconstruction de la vue** (changement de contexte) pendant l'attente : l'attente est perdue sans mot ; le SIGTERM reste envoyé. `Running()` protège seulement le cas `OriginView`. Limite documentée.
538	- **Routeur** : le `case netdiag.BackgroundMsg` change le chemin de `portsKillResultMsg` (correction d'un défaut existant : ligne busy à vie si on quitte `:net`) ; risque de régression faible, couvert par l'étape 6.
539	- **Exception Rule 130** (grisé pour une opération en cours) imposée par le critère 7 ; à écrire, sinon un relecteur la prendra pour une dérive.
540	- **En-tête à 80 colonnes** : une entrée de plus (`esc`) sur l'onglet Ports ; vérifier à la main que `K` reste visible à 80 colonnes (aucun test de mise en page d'en-tête n'est prévu ici).
541	- **Préexistant, hors périmètre** : la modale Windows de S-02a (ligne de 89 cellules) déborde à 80 colonnes ; S-02a doit rester inchangée → proposer un bug séparé.
542	- **Fenêtre résiduelle** macOS / Linux sans pidfd (D-C) : s'applique maintenant à deux signaux au lieu d'un ; inchangée en nature.
543	- **Sonde par PID** : entre deux sondes le PID peut être repris ; l'identité le détecte (`ProcessExited`), donc annonce « stopped » — vrai pour le processus visé.
544	
545	**Irréversible.** Rien de persistant : aucun schéma, cache ni configuration. Côté utilisateur, un SIGTERM envoyé ne se rappelle pas (assumé par le critère 4 et dit à `esc`). L'API interne (`osProcs.kill` à trois arguments, `Terminate`, `Probe`) se défait par un revert.

516	## 5. Ce qui est testable, et comment
517	
518	| Domaine | Linux (CI) | macOS | Windows |
519	|---|---|---|---|
520	| Décisions pures (`parseStat`, zombies, `livenessOf`, `signalTarget`) | tests unitaires | mêmes fonctions, testées sous Linux | idem |
521	| `Terminate` / `Kill` / `Probe` par seams | `fakeOS`, aucun signal | compilation croisée (`go test -c`) | compilation croisée ; `goos = "windows"` testé sous Linux |
522	| Signaux réels | enfants du test (`allowRealSignals`) : SIGTERM, SIGKILL, refus d'identité, zombie réel | **non exécuté** : `readStatus` darwin lu, compilé, pas lancé | non concerné (aucun SIGTERM) |
523	| Machine à états UI | injection de messages, `processOps` faux | identique (le code UI ne dépend pas de l'OS hors `ops.windows`) | `installProcs(m, true)` |
524	| Routage hors écran | `internal/app`, `Cmd` non exécutés | — | — |
525	
526	## 6. Hypothèses, risques, irréversible
527	
528	**Hypothèses non vérifiées.**
529	- H1 : un zombie Linux garde `starttime` dans `/proc/<pid>/stat` (proc(5)) — vérifié par `TestProbeSeesARealZombie`.
530	- H2 : sous macOS, `kern.proc.pid` rend un zombie avec `P_stat == SZOMB (5)` et son `P_starttime`. Non exécuté. Si faux, le zombie se lit « parti » : compté arrêté dans les deux cas.
531	- H3 : `darwinSZOMB = 5` (valeur de `<sys/proc.h>`, non exportée par `x/sys`).
532	- H4 : sous macOS, SIP peut refuser SIGTERM → `EPERM` → message existant (critère 6).
533	- H5 : `tea.Tick` appelle son callback dans la goroutine du `Cmd` (la sonde y est faite) — conforme à l'usage actuel de bubbletea v2.
534	
535	**Risques.**
536	- **Modale hors de vue** : l'échéance peut ouvrir la 2e confirmation pendant que l'utilisateur est sur un autre onglet ou une autre vue ; il la retrouve sur Ports. Rien n'est forcé sans elle (critère 3 tenu), mais l'utilisateur peut ne pas savoir qu'elle attend. Limite documentée.
537	- **Reconstruction de la vue** (changement de contexte) pendant l'attente : l'attente est perdue sans mot ; le SIGTERM reste envoyé. `Running()` protège seulement le cas `OriginView`. Limite documentée.
538	- **Routeur** : le `case netdiag.BackgroundMsg` change le chemin de `portsKillResultMsg` (correction d'un défaut existant : ligne busy à vie si on quitte `:net`) ; risque de régression faible, couvert par l'étape 6.
539	- **Exception Rule 130** (grisé pour une opération en cours) imposée par le critère 7 ; à écrire, sinon un relecteur la prendra pour une dérive.
540	- **En-tête à 80 colonnes** : une entrée de plus (`esc`) sur l'onglet Ports ; vérifier à la main que `K` reste visible à 80 colonnes (aucun test de mise en page d'en-tête n'est prévu ici).
541	- **Préexistant, hors périmètre** : la modale Windows de S-02a (ligne de 89 cellules) déborde à 80 colonnes ; S-02a doit rester inchangée → proposer un bug séparé.
542	- **Fenêtre résiduelle** macOS / Linux sans pidfd (D-C) : s'applique maintenant à deux signaux au lieu d'un ; inchangée en nature.
543	- **Sonde par PID** : entre deux sondes le PID peut être repris ; l'identité le détecte (`ProcessExited`), donc annonce « stopped » — vrai pour le processus visé.
544	
545	**Irréversible.** Rien de persistant : aucun schéma, cache ni configuration. Côté utilisateur, un SIGTERM envoyé ne se rappelle pas (assumé par le critère 4 et dit à `esc`). L'API interne (`osProcs.kill` à trois arguments, `Terminate`, `Probe`) se défait par un revert.
546	
547	## 7. Questions (non bloquantes ; défauts appliqués, à valider par l'utilisateur)
548	
549	1. **Q2** : 5 s fixe, non configurable — défaut appliqué (`stopGrace`).
550	2. **Q6** : `K` « Stop process » sous Linux/macOS, « Kill process » sous Windows — défaut appliqué (3.4).
551	3. Zombie compté arrêté ; un seul arrêt en attente ; `esc` ne signale rien — défauts appliqués.
552	4. Textes proposés hors critères : refus de la 2e confirmation `nginx (812) left running — no SIGKILL sent` ; grisé sur la ligne même `This process is already being stopped` ; `nginx (812) stopped` quand le processus est sorti entre l'échéance et le `Yes` du SIGKILL.
553	5. Une ligne absente du tableau à la 2e confirmation est quand même forcée (identité revérifiée au signal) — défaut appliqué, l'inverse laisserait sans recours un processus qui a fermé ses sockets sans sortir.

208	// matchPortTokens applies the toggle filters: OR within a group, AND between
209	// them. `numeric` and `paused` are shown in the bar but filter nothing — they
210	// report a mode, which is why they are not consulted here.
211	func matchPortTokens(p ports.Socket, active map[string]bool) bool {
212		return matchesActive(p.Protocol, active, filterTokenTCP, filterTokenUDP) &&

216	// matchesActive reports whether value equals one of the labels the user turned
217	// on. A group with nothing on does not filter: that is "no opinion", not
218	// "match nothing", and getting the two confused would empty the table on open.
219	func matchesActive(value string, active map[string]bool, labels ...string) bool {
220		anyOn := false
221		for _, label := range labels {
222			if !active[label] {
223				continue
224			}
225			anyOn = true
226			if strings.EqualFold(value, label) {
227				return true
228			}
229		}
230		return !anyOn
231	}

348	}

350	// identityChangedText is what the footer says when the PID is held by another
351	// process than the one that was listed: nothing was sent and the table is read
352	// again (DEVDESK-709, S-01b criterion 2). A process with no name reads by its
353	// PID alone.
354	func identityChangedText(process, pid string) string {
355		who := "PID " + pid
356		if process != "" {
357			who = process + " (PID " + pid + ")"
358		}
359		return who + " is no longer the process that was listed — table refreshed"
360	}
361	
362	// refusal is the one place a refused or failed stop becomes a footer line: the
363	// press of K (the confirmation's read), Yes (the table compared with the
364	// target) and the kill's result all come here, so one error reads the same
365	// wherever it surfaces. errors.As comes first: DevDesk's own refusals are
366	// typed, and the system's sentinels are read last (killFailureMessage).
367	//
368	// The three typed refusals are preconditions, a Warn (Rule 128): the action
369	// cannot be honored as requested, nothing failed. They print their own
370	// Error(), taken from the extracted error so the "killing process N:" prefix
371	// ports.Kill adds never reaches the screen.
372	func (pm *PortsModel) refusal(pid, process string, err error) tea.Cmd {
373		var protected *ports.ProtectedError
374		var changed *ports.IdentityChangedError
375		var unverifiable *ports.UnverifiableError
376		switch {
377		case errors.As(err, &protected):
378			return pm.footer.Warn(protected.Error())
379		case errors.As(err, &changed):
380			// Another process holds the PID: nothing was sent, and the table is read
381			// again so the row on screen stops being the one that was listed.
382			return tea.Batch(pm.footer.Warn(identityChangedText(process, pid)), requestPortsRefresh())
383		case errors.As(err, &unverifiable):
384			// The cause is the system's, for the log; the screen says DevDesk's.
385			log.Printf("ERROR [netdiag/ports] identity pid=%s: %v (cause: %v)", pid, err, unverifiable.Cause)
386			return pm.footer.Warn(unverifiable.Error())
387		}
388		log.Printf("ERROR [netdiag/ports] ports.Kill pid=%s: %v", pid, err)
389		return pm.footer.Error(killFailureMessage(pid, err))
390	}
391	
392	// killFailureMessage says why the signal did not land.
393	//
394	// DevDesk signals with the rights it has (§3.43), so the refusal the user meets
395	// most often is the operating system's — another user's process, a service, one
396	// Windows protects. "Failed to kill PID 1234" gave them no reason to suspect
397	// that, and made "access denied" and "already gone" the same sentence.
398	//
399	// The platform error itself never reaches the screen: it comes back in the
400	// machine's own language — measured here, PID 4 answers `OpenProcess: Accès
401	// refusé.` — which is the route stage's rule (§3.44). errors.Is reads through
402	// the %w wrapping ports.Kill applies, and both sentinels are the standard
403	// library's.
404	//
405	// The permission branch was measured on Windows: killing PID 4 (System) gives
406	// ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, which syscall.Errno maps onto os.ErrPermission. EPERM
407	// maps the same way on Unix.
408	//
409	// The "already gone" branch fires on Unix, where ESRCH maps to
410	// os.ErrProcessDone. On Windows, OpenProcess on a PID that does not exist fails
411	// with ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER, which syscall.Errno maps to neither sentinel;
412	// internal/ports (identity_windows.go, procos.go) now maps it to
413	// os.ErrProcessDone, but that mapping has not been confirmed on a real Windows
414	// host (DEVDESK-727). Until it is, the message may still fall to the generic
415	// one there, and the row disappears on the next two-second refresh anyway.
416	func killFailureMessage(pid string, err error) string {
417		switch {
418		case errors.Is(err, os.ErrPermission):
419			return fmt.Sprintf("Refused by the system — DevDesk cannot signal PID %s", pid)
420		case errors.Is(err, os.ErrProcessDone):
421			return fmt.Sprintf("PID %s is no longer running", pid)
422		}
423		return fmt.Sprintf("Failed to kill PID %s — check logs", pid)
424	}
425	
426	func (pm *PortsModel) handleKey(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
427		if pm.confirmModal != nil {
428			var cmd tea.Cmd
429			pm.confirmModal, cmd = pm.confirmModal.Update(msg)
430			return pm, cmd
431		}
432		if pm.table.InEditMode() {
433			cmd := pm.table.Update(msg)
434			pm.table.GotoTop() // a narrowing query starts from the first match
435			return pm, cmd
436		}
437		return pm.handleKeyNormal(msg)
438	}
439	
440	// handlePaste gives pasted text to the filter bar while it has the keyboard and
441	// no modal is open; otherwise it is dropped (Rule 111).
442	func (pm *PortsModel) handlePaste(msg tea.PasteMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
443		if pm.confirmModal != nil || !pm.table.InEditMode() {
444			return pm, nil
445		}
446		cmd := pm.table.Update(msg)
447		pm.table.GotoTop() // a narrowing query starts from the first match
448		return pm, cmd
449	}
450	
451	// toggleToken flips a filter and returns to the top, since the list under the
452	// cursor is not the list the user was looking at any more.
453	func (pm *PortsModel) toggleToken(label string) {
454		pm.table.SetTokenActive(label, !pm.table.IsTokenActive(label))
455		pm.table.GotoTop()
456	}
457	
458	func (pm *PortsModel) handleKeyNormal(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
459		switch msg.String() {
460		case "up", "down", "pgup", "pgdown", "home", "end", "/":
461			return pm, pm.table.Update(msg)
462		case keymap.Space:
463			pm.paused = !pm.paused
464			pm.table.SetTokenActive(filterTokenPaused, pm.paused)
465			// Pausing is a state, not an event: it is derived in statusLine rather
466			// than set as a message, which would expire while still paused.
467		case "t":
468			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenTCP)
469		case "u":
470			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenUDP)
471		case "l":
472			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenListen)
473		case "e":
474			pm.toggleToken(filterTokenEstab)
475		case "n":
476			pm.numericAddrs = !pm.numericAddrs
477			pm.table.SetTokenActive(filterTokenNumeric, pm.numericAddrs)
478			return pm, fetchPortsCmd(pm.numericAddrs)
479		case "z":
480			for _, label := range []string{
481				filterTokenTCP, filterTokenUDP, filterTokenListen, filterTokenEstab, filterTokenPaused,
482			} {
483				pm.table.SetTokenActive(label, false)
484			}
485			pm.table.FilterBar().ClearSearch()
486			pm.table.SetItems(pm.table.Items()) // re-apply with the query gone
487			pm.paused = false
488			pm.table.GotoTop()
489		case keymap.Kill:
490			return pm.confirmKill()
491		}
492		return pm, nil
493	}
494	
495	// confirmKill asks before sending the signal.
496	//
497	// This is the one action in the application that reaches outside it: not a
498	// container to be brought back up, but a process belonging to whoever is at
499	// this machine, killed with SIGKILL so it gets no chance to save anything. It
500	// had no confirmation at all, while deleting a container — recreatable from its
501	// image — had one (§3.26).
502	func (pm *PortsModel) confirmKill() (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
503		if k := pm.killable(); !k.Enabled() {
504			return pm, pm.footer.Warn(k.Reason)
505		}
506		entry, _ := pm.table.Selected()
507		if pm.table.IsBusy(entry.PID) {
508			return pm, pm.footer.Warn("Already killing PID " + entry.PID)
509		}
510		// A deferred identity (Windows, over the listing budget) is read here, in
511		// Update, one short read at the press of K and never at render. Any refusal
512		// shows now, with no confirmation to answer first (DEVDESK-709).
513		identity, err := pm.ops.confirm(entry.PID, entry.Identity)
514		if err != nil {
515			return pm, pm.refusal(entry.PID, entry.Process, err)
516		}
517		// The target is captured here, once, as values: the table refreshes every
518		// two seconds and the cursor stays on an index, so by the time the user
519		// answers, the selected row can be another process (DEVDESK-714).
520		target := killTarget{PID: entry.PID, Process: entry.Process, Identity: identity}
521		pm.pendingKill = &target
522		pm.confirmModal = components.NewConfirmModal("Kill Process", killPrompt(target, pm.ops.windows))
523		return pm, nil
524	}
525	
526	// killTarget is the process a confirmation is about: what the user was shown
527	// when it opened, whatever the table does afterwards.
528	type killTarget struct {
529		PID      string
530		Process  string
531		Identity ports.Identity // the one the row was listed with, or read when the confirmation opened (DEVDESK-709)
532	}
533	
534	// killPrompt is the text of the confirmation. Windows has no signal to send:
535	// the process is ended at once, so the sentence says that instead of naming
536	// a SIGKILL that does not exist there.
537	func killPrompt(t killTarget, windows bool) string {
538		if windows {
539			return fmt.Sprintf("Terminate %s (PID %s)?\n\nWindows has no clean stop for this process: it is ended at once and cannot save anything.",
540				t.Process, t.PID)
541		}
542		return fmt.Sprintf("Send SIGKILL to %s (PID %s)?\n\nThe process gets no chance to shut down cleanly.",
543			t.Process, t.PID)
544	}
545	
546	// killHelpDescription is the help line of K on the Ports tab.
547	func killHelpDescription(windows bool) string {
548		if windows {
549			return "End the selected process at once, after confirmation (Ports tab)"
550		}
551		return "Send SIGKILL to the selected process, after confirmation (Ports tab)"
552	}
553	
554	// presence says what the last table received holds of a kill target.
555	type presence int
556	
557	const (
558		// present: a row of the target's PID has its name and no conflicting identity.
559		present presence = iota
560		// replaced: a row holds the target's PID under another identity, so another
561		// process has it now and nothing may be sent (DEVDESK-709, criterion 2).
562		replaced
563		// absent: no row holds the PID. The process may be gone, or its PID may
564		// belong to another process under another name (D174).
565		absent
566	)
567	
568	// targetPresence compares the target with the last table received, without a
569	// system call. A deferred or unknown identity never conflicts (Conflicts needs
570	// both known): the signal itself verifies those against the process it holds.
571	func (pm *PortsModel) targetPresence(t killTarget) presence {
572		result := absent
573		for _, s := range pm.table.Items() {
574			switch {
575			case s.PID != t.PID:
576			case s.Identity.Conflicts(t.Identity):
577				result = replaced
578			case s.Process == t.Process:
579				return present
580			}
581		}
582		return result
583	}
584	
585	// Why K does not apply, written once so the header, the footer and the tests
586	// cannot drift apart on the wording (Rule 129 — English US).
587	const (
588		reasonNoSocketRow = "No socket selected"
589		reasonNoPID       = "The system did not say which process holds this socket"
590		// reasonUnverifiable greys K on a row DevDesk could not read an identity for
591		// (DEVDESK-709, S-01b criterion 4): without it a signal could land on
592		// whatever process holds the PID by then.
593		reasonUnverifiable = "Cannot verify which process this is"
594	)
595	
596	// killable reports whether K has a process to signal (Rule 130).
597	//
598	// A protected process (DevDesk itself, the process that started it, PID 1, the
599	// Windows system processes) is greyed with the reason ports.Protection gives.
600	//
601	// A socket the system declines to attribute carries no PID — `List` blanks a
602	// PID of zero rather than printing it, because process 0 is a whole process
603	// group on Unix and a row reading "0" would look killable. That is the state
604	// this greys; whether the operating system will *accept* the signal is a
605	// different question, and one only the attempt can answer.
606	func (pm *PortsModel) killable() shortcut.Availability {
607		entry, ok := pm.table.Selected()
608		switch {
609		case !ok:
610			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoSocketRow)
611		case entry.PID == "":
612			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonNoPID)
613		}
614		if p := pm.ops.protection(entry.PID); p != ports.Unprotected {
615			return shortcut.Unavailable(p.Reason())
616		}
617		// After the protection, as in ports.Kill: DevDesk's own row says what it
618		// is, not that DevDesk cannot verify it. A deferred identity is verifiable:
619		// it is read when the confirmation opens, never here.
620		if !entry.Identity.Verifiable() {
621			return shortcut.Unavailable(reasonUnverifiable)
622		}
623		return shortcut.Availability{}
624	}
625	
626	// handleConfirmNo closes the confirmation without a signal.
627	func (pm *PortsModel) handleConfirmNo() (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
628		pm.confirmModal = nil
629		pm.pendingKill = nil
630		return pm, nil
631	}
632	
633	// handleConfirmYes sends the signal to the target captured when the
634	// confirmation opened, never to the row under the cursor. A Yes with no
635	// pending target (nothing was opened) does nothing. A target the last table no
636	// longer lists is refused with a warning (it may be gone, or its PID may belong
637	// to another process by now), and so is one the table lists under another
638	// identity, which says so and reads the table again.
639	func (pm *PortsModel) handleConfirmYes() (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd) {
640		target := pm.pendingKill
641		pm.confirmModal = nil
642		pm.pendingKill = nil
643		if target == nil {
644			return pm, nil
645		}
646		switch pm.targetPresence(*target) {
647		case replaced:
648			pid, _ := strconv.Atoi(target.PID)
649			return pm, pm.refusal(target.PID, target.Process, &ports.IdentityChangedError{PID: pid})
650		case absent:
651			return pm, pm.footer.Warn(fmt.Sprintf("%s (PID %s) is no longer listed — not stopped", target.Process, target.PID))
652		}
653		// The state may have changed since the confirmation opened; the verdict on
654		// the captured target decides, not the row under the cursor.
655		if p := pm.ops.protection(target.PID); p != ports.Unprotected {
656			return pm, pm.footer.Warn(fmt.Sprintf("PID %s not stopped: %s", target.PID, p.Reason()))
657		}
658		if pm.table.IsBusy(target.PID) {
659			return pm, nil
660		}
661		// Keyed on the PID, so every socket the process holds shows the running dot
662		// at once — which is what happens: the kill takes them all. The table reads
663		// the busy mark at render; the router's frame drives the blink.
664		pm.table.MarkBusy(target.PID, "Killing "+target.Process+" ("+target.PID+")")
665		return pm, killProcessCmd(pm.ops.kill, *target)
666	}
667	
668	// view renders the table. An empty table stays a table (Rule 139) — its
669	// header and no rows — whether it is genuinely empty, filtered down to
670	// nothing, still loading, or stale: those are a footer status (statusLine) and
671	// a header count, never body text.
672	func (pm *PortsModel) view() string {
673		return pm.table.View()
674	}
675	
676	// summaryLine counts what is on screen, for the header (Rule 139).
677	func (pm *PortsModel) summaryLine() string {
678		return fmt.Sprintf("%d", len(pm.table.Items()))
679	}

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in

    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP; a Proxy row says whether a proxy variable applies, the checks themselves stay direct, DEVDESK-582) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the five checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. `test-race` is the only test run (`-race` covers `go test`); `mise run test` stays available alone for the fast local loop. CI runs fmt-check, vet, lint and build in the `Lint and build` job and `test-race` in the `Test` job, on every pull request, docs-only ones included (the docs-only shortcut applies to `Lint and build` only); the whole CI targets under 10 minutes, so run this locally before a PR to catch a red check early

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`), the tab progress bar (OSC 9;4, `terminalProgress`), the window title (`windowTitle`, restored by `internal/termtitle`), the terminal hand-off to child processes (the exec wrapper `internal/ui/teaexec`, use it instead of `tea.ExecProcess`, D121) and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci` (typed `StatusError`, `...Context` variants), `internal/netproxy` (the proxy entry point every HTTP and TLS connection goes through, and its guard test, DEVDESK-581), the proxy passed to scanner containers (`netproxy.Forward`, `scan.containerRun.cmd`, the `TestContainerGuard*` guard, DEVDESK-583), `internal/imagesearch` and the registry browser's image search level, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface`, `internal/nettrace` (the path trace: unprivileged UDP + `IP_RECVERR` on Linux, ICMP echo through `iphlpapi` on native Windows) |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage`, `internal/ui/datatable`, and the activity indicator column (`internal/ui/indicator`, `datatable.IndicatorColumn`, the row sentences `components.DescribeRow`) |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |
| [`nexus-bench.md`](../docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md) | `internal/nexusbench` — the disposable Nexus Community bench on the k0s cluster (DEVDESK-504, NX-01; seed, DEVDESK-505; `cut-upstream`, `restore-upstream` and `reset`, DEVDESK-534; recorded fixtures `internal/nexusfixture` (campaigns `catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) and `nexus-bench record`, DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580): decisions, the `NEXUS_BENCH_*` parameters and their validation, manifests, preflight, deployment, provisioning, destruction, the `nexus-bench` command (`cmd/nexus-bench`) and its `mise run nexus-bench:*` tasks, the upstream cut, restore and reset, the recorded fixtures (format, redaction, the `fakenexus` replay server, `record`, the stale test), what is still to come (NX-03 onward); a development tool outside `mise run ci` |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv. The `TestMain` of `internal/app`
also replaces `detectTools` (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`, production value `scan.Detect`) with an
empty report, so `App.Init` never runs the `trivy`, `gitleaks` and `plumber` of the machine
(DEVDESK-645); `TestInitDoesNotRunTheScannersOfTheHost` and `TestDetectToolsIsScanDetectInProduction`
guard it.

**Tests and the host secret store (DEVDESK-610).** By default `credentials.Select` and
`KeyringAvailable` reach the real keyring of the machine (Secret Service over D-Bus on
Linux); a locked keyring blocks the whole suite until the timeout. A test binary that can
reach them isolates the store: `fakekeyring.Install()` in `TestMain`, then
`fakekeyring.Fresh(t)` (or `FreshUnreachable(t, err)` for a locked keyring) per test, from
`internal/testutil/fakekeyring`. `isolateHome(t)` already calls `Fresh` in `internal/app` and
`internal/ui/setup`. Two guards enforce it: at run time, any keyring or `git credential` call
in a test binary without the fake panics with `DEVDESK-610` and the operation; statically,
`TestHostStoreGuard*` (`internal/credentials/hoststore_guard_test.go`) fails on K1 (go-keyring
imported outside `internal/credentials`), K2 (`SwapHostStoreForTest` in non-test code) and K3
(`fakekeyring` imported by non-test code). The seam is `credentials.HostStore` and
`SwapHostStoreForTest`, reserved for tests (it panics outside a test binary). Limits: the
runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".

**Tests and real signals (DEVDESK-708).** A test must never signal a real process. In
`internal/ports` the only place that does is `realOS.kill` (`internal/ports/procos.go`),
reached through the `procOS` seam; `selfPID`, `parentPID` and `goos` are seams too. A test
substitutes them (`useFakeOS(t, self, parent, goos)` in `seams_test.go`), and in
`internal/ui/netdiag` it replaces `processOps` on the model, so `ports.Kill` is never reached.
Two guards enforce it: at run time, a real signal in a test binary panics with `DEVDESK-708`
unless the test called `allowRealSignals(t)`, which only a test that kills a child it
started itself may do (`TestKillEndsARealChildProcess`); statically, `TestOnlyRealOSSendsASignal`
fails on a signalling call (`os.FindProcess`, `syscall.Kill`, `unix.Kill`,
`windows.TerminateProcess`, `.Kill(` or `.Signal(`) outside `(realOS) kill`. Limits: the static
guard misses an aliased import, another package and an external binary; the seams are global, so
no `t.Parallel`. See `docs/architecture/network.md`, "Seams and the signal guard".

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)

- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state

router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)

- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). ## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the five checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. `test-race` is the only test run (`-race` covers `go test`); `mise run test` stays available alone for the fast local loop. CI runs fmt-check, vet, lint and build in the `Lint and build` job and `test-race` in the `Test` job, on every pull request, docs-only ones included (the docs-only shortcut applies to `Lint and build` only); the whole CI targets under 10 minutes, so run this locally before a PR to catch a red check early

```

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv. The `TestMain` of `internal/app`
also replaces `detectTools` (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`, production value `scan.Detect`) with an
empty report, so `App.Init` never runs the `trivy`, `gitleaks` and `plumber` of the machine
(DEVDESK-645); `TestInitDoesNotRunTheScannersOfTheHost` and `TestDetectToolsIsScanDetectInProduction`
guard it.

**Tests and the host secret store (DEVDESK-610).** By default `credentials.Select` and
`KeyringAvailable` reach the real keyring of the machine (Secret Service over D-Bus on
Linux); a locked keyring blocks the whole suite until the timeout. A test binary that can
reach them isolates the store: `fakekeyring.Install()` in `TestMain`, then
`fakekeyring.Fresh(t)` (or `FreshUnreachable(t, err)` for a locked keyring) per test, from
`internal/testutil/fakekeyring`. `isolateHome(t)` already calls `Fresh` in `internal/app` and
`internal/ui/setup`. Two guards enforce it: at run time, any keyring or `git credential` call
in a test binary without the fake panics with `DEVDESK-610` and the operation; statically,
`TestHostStoreGuard*` (`internal/credentials/hoststore_guard_test.go`) fails on K1 (go-keyring
imported outside `internal/credentials`), K2 (`SwapHostStoreForTest` in non-test code) and K3
(`fakekeyring` imported by non-test code). The seam is `credentials.HostStore` and
`SwapHostStoreForTest`, reserved for tests (it panics outside a test binary). Limits: the
runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".

**Tests and real signals (DEVDESK-708).** A test must never signal a real process. In
`internal/ports` the only place that does is `realOS.kill` (`internal/ports/procos.go`),
reached through the `procOS` seam; `selfPID`, `parentPID` and `goos` are seams too. A test
substitutes them (`useFakeOS(t, self, parent, goos)` in `seams_test.go`), and in
`internal/ui/netdiag` it replaces `processOps` on the model, so `ports.Kill` is never reached.
Two guards enforce it: at run time, a real signal in a test binary panics with `DEVDESK-708`
unless the test called `allowRealSignals(t)`, which only a test that kills a child it
started itself may do (`TestKillEndsARealChildProcess`); statically, `TestOnlyRealOSSendsASignal`
fails on a signalling call (`os.FindProcess`, `syscall.Kill`, `unix.Kill`,
`windows.TerminateProcess`, `.Kill(` or `.Signal(`) outside `(realOS) kill`. Limits: the static
guard misses an aliased import, another package and an external binary; the seams are global, so
no `t.Parallel`. See `docs/architecture/network.md`, "Seams and the signal guard".

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
